expires_at.description: When the token stops working, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in the future and within the organization's cap on token age; absent or empty creates a token with no expiry of its own.

name.description: The token's display name, required, at most 100 bytes.

created_at.description: When the token was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

effective_expires_at.description: When the token stops working, as an RFC 3339 timestamp: the earlier of expires_at and the organization's current cap on token age, or null when neither applies.

expires_at.description: The expiry asked for when the token was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, or null when none was.

last_used_at.description: When the token last authenticated a request, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, or null when it never has.

org_id.description: The id of the organization the token acts in, fixed when it was created.

token.description: The token itself, sent as a Bearer credential. It is returned only here, never by a later read.

effective_expires_at.description: When the token stops working, as an RFC 3339 timestamp: the earlier of expires_at and the organization's current cap on token age, or null when neither applies.

last_used_at.description: When the token last authenticated a request, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, or null when it never has.

org_id.description: The id of the organization the token acts in, fixed when it was created.

token_prefix.description: The first eleven characters of the token, which tell two tokens apart.

org_id.description: Keeps only the tokens for this organization. Absent or empty keeps the tokens for every organization, except in a request made with an API token, which reads only its own organization's tokens.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

sort_dir.description: The order's direction, asc or desc; it needs sort_key.

sort_key.description: What to order by: last_used_at or created_at, newest first by default. A token never used sorts last under last_used_at in either direction. Absent orders by creation, newest first.

max_age_days.description: The most days an API token in the organization may live, counted from its creation, or null when there is no cap.

name.description: The token's new display name, at most 100 bytes. It cannot be cleared, and a body without it, or with null, is refused.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

default_github_host.description: The base URL of the GitHub that Sign in with GitHub uses, such as https://github.com.

deployment_mode.description: How this deployment runs: local for one person on their own machine, or multi for a shared deployment with sign-in.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

email.description: The email address to invite, which the invitee must hold verified to accept; it is stored in lower case.

role.description: The role the invitee takes in the organization: admin or member, member when absent or empty.

target_team_id.description: The id of a team in the organization the invitee also joins, as a member; absent or empty invites to the organization alone.

accept_url.description: The link the invitee opens to accept, which carries the invite's secret token. It is returned only here, never by a later read.

expires_at.description: When the invite stops being redeemable, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, seven days after it was created.

cve_id.description: The advisory's CVE id, absent when it has none.

first_patched_version.description: The first version that fixes the advisory, absent when none has been released.

ghsa_id.description: The advisory's GitHub Security Advisory id.

manifest_path.description: The path of the manifest file that declares the package.

number.description: The alert's number in its repository.

scope.description: Whether the dependency is runtime or development, absent when GitHub does not know.

severity.description: The advisory's severity: low, medium, high, or critical.

summary.description: The advisory's summary, to be shown as plain text, absent when the advisory has none.

vulnerable_version_range.description: The range of versions the advisory affects, absent when GitHub reports none.

features.description: The Enterprise features licensed for the caller's current organization, such as governance; empty when none is.

errors.description: Every fault found in the request, at least one.

field.description: The request field at fault, present only when the fault is in one field.

message.description: A description of the fault for a person to read.

reason.description: A stable machine code for the fault, in upper snake case, such as INVALID_FIELD.

configured.description: Whether the organization exists; false in local mode until it is created, and always true in multi mode.

github.description: Whether the organization holds a GitHub personal access token.

github_ready.description: Whether the organization has GitHub access it can use, through a personal access token or a GitHub App.

github_repos.description: How many repositories on the organization's GitHub host at least one of its teams tracks.

github_url.description: The base URL of the organization's GitHub, absent when none is set.

jira.description: Whether the organization holds a usable Jira credential.

jira_deployment.description: Which kind of Jira the organization's credential is for, cloud or data_center, present only when jira is true.

jira_url.description: The base URL of the organization's Jira site, absent when none is set.

linear.description: Whether the organization holds a usable Linear credential.

linear_workspace_url_key.description: The URL key of the Linear workspace the organization's credential belongs to, absent when none is recorded.

setup_complete.description: Whether setup is finished: GitHub access is configured, a team tracks at least one repository, and in multi mode the background-jobs model and the default team's model are chosen.

setup_step.description: Where an unfinished setup resumes: org for the organization's GitHub access or background-jobs model, team for the default team's repositories or model, or done.

token.description: The token from the invite's accept link.

org_id.description: The id of the organization the caller joined, which is now the session's current organization.

email.description: The invited email address, in lower case.

expires_at.description: When the invite stops being redeemable, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

invited_by.description: The user id of the admin who created the invite, absent when it is not recorded.

role.description: The role the invitee takes in the organization: admin or member.

target_team_id.description: The id of the team the invitee also joins, absent for an invite to the organization alone.

expires_at.description: When the invite stops being redeemable, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when status is not_found.

invited_by_name.description: The display name of the admin who created the invite, absent when status is not_found or none is recorded.

org_name.description: The name of the organization the invite is to, absent when status is not_found.

role.description: The role the invitee takes in the organization, admin or member, absent when status is not_found.

status.description: Whether the invite can be accepted: valid, expired, revoked, accepted, or not_found when no invite has the token.

current.description: Whether this is the identity the request's session signed in with.

email.description: The email address the identity carries, absent when it has none.

email_verified.description: Whether the identity's email address is verified.

idp.description: The identity provider behind a saml identity: entra, okta, google, onelogin, ping, or other. Absent for other providers and when it is not known.

linked_at.description: When the identity was linked to the person, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC; absent in local mode.

login.description: The GitHub login of a github identity, absent for other providers and when it is not recorded.

provider.description: How the person signs in with this identity: github, saml for single sign-on, or local for the one local-mode user.

methods.description: Every identity linked to the caller, oldest first.

role.description: The caller's role in the organization: owner, admin, or member.

sso_required.description: Whether the organization requires its own single sign-on and this request's credential did not come through it, in which case every request about the organization is refused with SSO_REQUIRED.

sso_start_url.description: Where the organization's single sign-on begins, present only when sso_required is true.

active_org_id.description: The id of the organization this request acts in: the session's current organization, or the one an API token was created for. Absent when there is none, or the caller no longer belongs to it.

avatar_url.description: The URL of the caller's avatar image, absent when none is recorded.

can_create_org.description: Whether this caller may create an organization: the deployment allows it, the request comes from a session rather than an API token, and the session signed in with GitHub rather than single sign-on.

display_name.description: The caller's display name, absent when none is recorded.

is_operator.description: Whether the caller is one of the deployment's operators; always true in local mode.

linear_display_name.description: The name Linear gives the user linear_user_id names, absent when none is recorded.

org_creation_enabled.description: Whether this deployment allows anyone to create an organization.

orgs.description: Every organization the caller belongs to, ordered by name; empty when they belong to none.

teams.description: Every active team the caller is a member of, in every organization they belong to, ordered by organization id and then team name; empty when they are on none.

role.description: The member's new role in the organization: owner, admin, or member.

github_username.description: The member's GitHub login on the organization's GitHub host, or null when they have none there.

jira_account_id.description: The member's Jira account id on the organization's Jira site, or null when they have none there.

linear_user_id.description: The member's Linear user id in the organization's Linear workspace, or null when they have none there.

role.description: The member's role in the organization: owner, admin, or member.

disabled.description: Whether the source is turned off for the organization: true turns it off, and false or null turns it back on.

sources.description: Every event source this deployment carries, each with its state for the organization.

bucket.description: The budget the service meters separately for the credential, such as core or graphql on GitHub, or a Slack method.

credential.description: The id of the credential the budget is metered against, such as pat or installation:123; never a token, a login, or a user id.

limit.description: The budget's size, or null when the service did not say.

near_limit.description: Whether the service said the budget is close to its limit, on a reading that states no count, such as Jira Cloud's hourly quota; null on every other reading.

observed_at.description: When the reading was taken, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

remaining.description: How many requests the budget had left, or null when the service did not say.

reset_at.description: When the budget refills, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, or null when the service did not say.

upstream.description: The service the budget is on, such as github, jira, linear, or slack.

used.description: How many requests Triage Factory counted itself making against the budget in its window, on a service that states no budget, such as Slack; null on a reading the service stated.

readings.description: The latest reading of each rate-limit budget of each of the organization's credentials, leaving out a reading past its reset time, or with no reset time and taken more than an hour ago.

base_branch.description: The branch agents base their work on, absent when they use the default branch.

can_edit.description: Whether the caller may change the repository's settings.

clone_error.description: The output of the failed clone, present only when clone_status is failed.

clone_error_kind.description: What kind of failure the clone hit, ssh or other, present only when clone_status is failed.

clone_status.description: The state of the repository's clone: pending until a clone attempt finishes, then ok or failed.

default_branch.description: The repository's default branch on GitHub, absent before it is profiled.

description.description: The repository's description on GitHub, absent when it has none.

github_id.description: GitHub's id for the repository, empty while it is not yet known.

has_agents_md.description: Whether the repository has an AGENTS.md.

has_claude_md.description: Whether the repository has a CLAUDE.md.

has_readme.description: Whether the repository has a README.

id.description: The repository's id in Triage Factory.

owner.description: The account that owns the repository on GitHub.

profile_text.description: A description of the repository written when it was profiled, absent before then.

profiled_at.description: When the repository was last profiled, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent before then.

repo.description: The repository's name without its owner.

slug.description: The repository's full name, as owner/name.

disableable.description: Whether an organization admin may turn the source off; GitHub cannot be turned off.

kind.description: The event source, such as github, jira, linear, or slack.

state.description: Whether the organization can receive events from the source: available; unconfigured when it lacks the setup the source needs; disabled when an organization admin turned it off; unlicensed when the deployment's licence does not include it; or wip when Triage Factory does not support it yet.

ai_summary.description: A summary of the task written when it was scored, absent before then.

autonomy_suitability.description: How suitable the task is for an agent to work without a person, from 0 to 1, or null before the task is scored.

can_write.description: Whether the caller may update, claim, delegate, or requeue the task, present on the task reads and absent from a write's response or when the check fails.

claim_team_ids.description: The ids of the teams the caller's claim or delegation may put the task on, in order, present on the single-task read only and absent when that read fails.

claimed_by_agent_id.description: The id of the agent that holds the task, absent when no agent does.

claimed_by_user_id.description: The id of the person who holds the task, absent when no person does.

close_reason.description: Why the task closed, such as run_completed, user_completed, user_dismissed, or auto_closed_by_event, absent while it is open.

conversation_id.description: The id of the task's current conversation, absent when nobody holds the task or its run has not started.

created_at.description: When the task was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

dedup_key.description: The value that tells apart tasks of one event type on one entity, such as a label name, absent for most event types.

entity_id.description: The id of the entity the task is about: a pull request, an issue, a vulnerable package, or a Slack thread or message.

entity_kind.description: The kind of entity the task is about: pr, issue, vulnerable_package, thread, or message.

event_type.description: The event type that created the task, such as github:pr:review_requested.

memory_attempt.description: The newest attempt to write that memory, absent when none has run.

memory_pending.description: Whether a conversation on the task ended without the memory the next conversation needs, in which case no further conversation on the task starts until that memory exists.

open_subtask_count.description: How many open subtasks the task's Jira issue has, 0 for any other entity.

priority_reasoning.description: The reasoning behind priority_score, absent before the task is scored.

priority_score.description: How urgently the task needs a person's attention, from 0 to 1, or null before the task is scored.

relevance_reason.description: Why the task concerns the person it was routed to, one of review_requested, authored, mentioned, and assigned, absent when none applies.

requested_reviewer.description: On a github:pr:review_requested task, the requested user's login or the requested team's org/slug, absent on every other task.

scoring_status.description: Where the task is in priority scoring: pending, in_progress, or scored.

severity.description: The task's severity, absent when none is recorded.

snooze_until.description: When a snoozed task returns to the queue, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when the task is not snoozed.

source.description: The system the task's entity comes from, such as github or jira.

source_id.description: The entity's key in its source, such as owner/repo#42 for a pull request or PROJ-123 for a Jira issue.

source_url.description: The entity's page in its source.

status.description: The task's lane: queued, in_progress, done, dismissed, or snoozed.

team_id.description: The id of the team that owns the task, absent while no single team owns it.

version.description: The task's version, which a write to the task must send and which each write raises.

vulnerable_package.description: The package and its open Dependabot alerts on a task whose entity_kind is vulnerable_package, absent on every other task.

closed_since.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp that limits done and dismissed tasks to those closed at or after it.

created_before.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp that limits the result to tasks created at or before it.

created_since.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp that limits the result to tasks created at or after it.

entity_kinds.description: Entity kinds whose tasks to include, such as pr or vulnerable_package; empty includes every kind.

event_types.description: Event types whose tasks to include, from the catalog GET /api/event-types returns; empty includes every event type.

ids.description: Ids of the tasks to include, at most 200, each a UUID in lowercase hyphenated form; empty includes every task.

include_snoozed.description: Whether to include tasks still inside their snooze window.

only_unclaimed.description: Whether to include only tasks nobody holds.

page_size.description: How many rows to return, 50 when absent; 0 returns no rows and only total_count, and a value above the list's maximum, 200 unless the route says otherwise, is refused.

page_token.description: The next_page_token of the previous page, which reads the page after it; it is refused for a request with different filters.

search.description: Text the task's title, source id, summary, or event type must contain, matched without regard to case.

sort_dir.description: The direction of sort_key, asc or desc, desc when absent; it is refused without sort_key.

sort_key.description: Orders the result by title, created, event_type, or claimee; absent orders it by the default, open tasks needing attention first and then by priority.

sources.description: Sources whose tasks to include, such as github or jira; empty includes every source.

statuses.description: Lanes to include, from queued, in_progress, done, dismissed, and snoozed; empty includes every lane.

team_ids.description: Ids of the teams whose tasks to include; empty includes every team the caller belongs to.

open_alert_count.description: How many alerts are open on the package.

active.description: Whether this is the connection the organization uses in the workspace, which is the one whose events are processed.

app_name.description: The Slack app's bot name, empty when Slack gave none.

bot_user_id.description: The Slack user id of the app's bot.

connection.description: The app's live Socket Mode connection status, absent for an app that receives events over HTTP and before the first connection attempt.

connected_at.description: When the connection last opened, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when it has not.

consecutive_failures.description: How many connection attempts in a row have failed.

last_error.description: The error of the last failed attempt, absent when there is none.

last_event_at.description: When the connection last received an event, as an RFC 3339 timestamp, absent when it has not.

sightings.description: Workspaces the app received events from that have no connection in the organization, absent when there are none.

count.description: How many events arrived from the workspace.

last_seen.description: When the last of them arrived, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

state.description: The connection's state: dialing, open, draining, backing_off, or auth_failed.

created_at.description: When the connection was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

enterprise_id.description: The id of the Enterprise Grid organization the workspace belongs to, absent for a standalone workspace.

registered_by_user_id.description: The id of the person who connected the app, absent when that person has since been removed.

source.description: Whose Slack app the connection is through: org for an app the organization created, or deployment for the deployment's own app.

transport.description: How Slack delivers the app's events, socket or events_api, or null on a deployment connection, which uses the transport the deployment configures.

updated_at.description: When the connection was last changed, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

session.description: The session cookie a browser sign-in sets. A deployment served over plain HTTP names it sid.
session.name: __Host-sid

token.description: An API token, sent as Authorization: Bearer tf_….

post.description: Ends the session the request's cookie names, closes that session's event streams, and clears the cookie. A request with no live session changes nothing and still succeeds, and an API token is refused because it has no session to end. Multi mode only.

Ends every session the caller holds, on every device, closes all of their event streams, and clears this request's cookie. API tokens are not sessions: a token request is refused, and the caller's tokens keep working. Multi mode only.

get.description: Returns the avatar image of a person in the caller's organization. The image is fetched from the address the person's sign-in provider gave and cached for a short time.

Returns the deployment facts a client needs before anyone signs in: whether it runs in local or multi mode, and which GitHub its sign-in uses. It needs no credential and says nothing about any person or organization.
Returns the Enterprise features licensed for the caller's current organization, as one unpaged list. A build with no licence answers an empty list.
Reports status ok once the server accepts requests. It needs no credential and checks no database or integration, so it says only that the process is serving.
get.summary: Check that the server is up

get.description: Reports which of GitHub, Jira, and Linear the caller's current organization has credentials for, how many repositories its teams track, and whether setup is complete and where it resumes. It reads stored state and calls none of those services.

post.description: Creates an invite to the caller's current organization for an email address and returns its accept link, which is shown only in this response. It sends no email; the caller passes the link on. Only an organization admin may call it, and an address with an invite pending or that belongs to a member is refused. Multi mode only.

Redeems an invite's token: the caller joins its organization with its role, and its team when it names one, and the organization becomes the session's current one. The caller must hold the invited email address verified, and an API token is refused. A caller who is already a member is not given the invite's role. Multi mode only.

Returns one page of the caller's current organization's invites that can still be accepted: not accepted, revoked, or expired. No row carries an invite's token or accept link. Only an organization admin may call it. Multi mode only.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

get.description: Returns the organization, role, and inviter of the invite a token belongs to, and whether it can still be accepted. It needs no credential, because the token is the invite's secret, and an unknown token answers status not_found. Multi mode only.

parameters.description: The token from the invite's accept link.
parameters.name: token

get.summary: Preview an invite by its token

get.description: Returns one of the caller's current organization's invites that can still be accepted, without its token or accept link. An accepted, revoked, or expired invite is not found. Only an organization admin may call it. Multi mode only.

post.description: Revokes an invite so its accept link stops working; revoking it again succeeds. An invite that was already accepted is refused. Only an organization admin may call it. Multi mode only.

get.description: Returns the caller's user id, their GitHub, Jira, and Linear identities, the organizations and teams they belong to with their role in each, the organization this request acts in, and whether they may create an organization. In local mode it describes the one local user.
get.summary: Get the caller's identity and memberships

post.description: Makes the named organization the current one for the caller's session, so the session's later requests act in it, and answers an empty object. An API token is refused, because its organization is fixed when it is created. Multi mode only.

get.description: Returns every identity the caller can sign in with, such as a GitHub account or a single sign-on login, oldest first, and marks the one this session signed in with. The list is not paged. In local mode it holds one identity with the provider local.

post.description: Creates an API token that acts as the caller in one organization they belong to, and returns it with its secret, which is shown only in this response. A request made with an API token may create one only in that token's own organization. Multi mode only.

Returns one page of the caller's API tokens, expired ones included and revoked ones left out, without their secrets. A request made with an API token reads only its own organization's tokens. Multi mode only.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

delete.description: Revokes one of the caller's API tokens so it stops working at once, including the token that makes the request. A request made with an API token may revoke only tokens in its own organization. Multi mode only.

patch.description: Sets one of the caller's API tokens' display name and returns the token. A request made with an API token may rename only tokens in its own organization. Multi mode only.

get.description: Returns the LLM spend of the runs the caller started in their current organization over the window, in USD, with its totals by category, model, and UTC day.

parameters.description: Start of the window, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight; with since and until both absent the window is the current UTC calendar month up to now, and with only one of them given the other end is open.
parameters.name: since

parameters.description: End of the window, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight, which must be after since when both are given.
parameters.name: until

post.description: In multi mode, creates an organization with its first team, makes the caller its owner and the team's admin, and makes it the session's current organization; it needs a session signed in with GitHub. In local mode it reads no body and creates the one local organization, answering 201 when it created it and 200 with already_provisioned true when it already existed.

get.description: Returns the organization's id and name, and the caller's role in it.
Returns the organization's cap on how long its API tokens may live, which binds every member's tokens. Multi mode only.
get.summary: Get an organization's API token policy

get.description: Returns, as one unpaged list, the latest reading of each rate-limit budget the organization's GitHub, Jira, Linear, and Slack credentials are metered against, taken from the responses to Triage Factory's own requests. It reads stored readings and calls none of those services.

post.description: Returns one page of the organization's members with their role and their GitHub, Jira, and Linear identities, ordered by display name, narrowed by search and excluding_team_id. Multi mode only.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

delete.description: Removes a person from the organization, ends their sessions and event streams in it, revokes their API tokens for it, and removes their Linear credential for its workspace, revoking it at Linear when it is an OAuth grant. A caller who names their own id leaves the organization, and its last owner cannot be removed. Multi mode only.

parameters.description: The id of the person to remove.
parameters.name: user_id

patch.description: Sets the member's role in the organization. The organization's last owner cannot be demoted. Multi mode only.

post.description: Returns one page of the organization's Slack connections, active and inactive, ordered by workspace name, then workspace id, then app id. Each connection carries its Socket Mode status when it has one.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

get.description: Returns, as one unpaged list, every event source this deployment carries, such as GitHub, Jira, and Linear, with whether the organization can receive events from it and, when it cannot, why. It says nothing about the organization's credentials.
Returns one event source with whether the organization can receive events from it and, when it cannot, why. A kind this deployment does not carry is not found.

parameters.description: The event source, such as github, jira, linear, or slack.
parameters.name: kind

get.summary: Get one of the organization's event sources

patch.description: Turns the source off or back on for the whole organization and returns its state. While it is off it is not polled, its events create no tasks, and no credential for it is used, but nothing is deleted: credentials, tasks, and event handlers stay as they are. Only an organization admin may call it, and GitHub cannot be turned off.

parameters.description: The event source, such as jira, linear, or slack.
parameters.name: kind

patch.summary: Turn an event source off or on

post.description: Returns one page of every active team in the organization, including teams the caller is not on, with the caller's role on the teams they belong to.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

post.description: Makes another member the organization's owner and makes the caller, its current owner, an admin. Only the owner may call it. Multi mode only.

get.description: Returns the organization's LLM spend over the window, in USD, with its totals by team, person, category, model, and UTC day, and the spend attributed to no team.

parameters.description: Start of the window, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight; with since and until both absent the window is the current UTC calendar month up to now, and with only one of them given the other end is open.
parameters.name: since

parameters.description: End of the window, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight, which must be after since when both are given.
parameters.name: until

patch.description: Sets or clears the branch agents base their work on in the repository, and returns the repository with the change applied.

parameters.description: The repository's id in Triage Factory.
parameters.name: id

post.description: Returns one page of the tasks the caller can see, narrowed by the body's filters and ordered by sort_key, or without one by attention and then priority. Each task says whether the caller may write it. A page_token resumes after the last task of the page that returned it, and is refused for different filters.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

post.description: Creates a team in the caller's current organization, gives it the shipped prompts, blueprints, and event handlers, makes the caller its admin, and returns it. Only an organization admin may call it. Multi mode only.
Returns one page of the archived teams in the caller's current organization. Only an organization admin may call it. Multi mode only.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

post.description: Returns one page of the active teams the caller belongs to in their current organization, each with the caller's role. In local mode it returns the one local team.

items.description: The rows of this page, as an empty array when it has none.

next_page_token.description: The page_token that reads the next page, absent on the last page.

total_count.description: How many rows match the request's filters across every page, or null for a list whose upstream cannot count them.

get.description: Returns one of the caller's organization's teams, archived or not, with the caller's role on it when they belong to it.

parameters.description: The team's id, or default for the one team in local mode.
parameters.name: team_id

patch.description: Sets the team's name, its description, or both, and returns the team with the change applied. Renaming derives a new slug from the name. A team admin or an organization admin may call it, and an archived team is refused. Multi mode only.
patch.summary: Rename a team or change its description

post.description: Archives the team, which hides it and refuses further changes to it, stops its agent runs in progress, and ends its conversations. It returns how many runs it stopped. Only an organization admin may call it, the organization's only active team cannot be archived, and an archived team is refused. Multi mode only.

get.description: Returns how many of the team's agent runs are in progress, which archiving it would stop, and whether it is already archived. Only an organization admin may call it. Multi mode only.
get.summary: Preview what archiving a team stops

post.description: Adds a member of the organization to the team with the given role. A person already on the team is refused. Multi mode only.

Returns one page of the team's members with their role and their GitHub, Jira, and Linear identities, ordered by display name and narrowed by search, and beside the page the organization's agent as the team has it configured. A page_token resumes after the page that returned it, and is refused for a different search.

parameters.description: The team's id, or default for the one team in local mode.
parameters.name: team_id

delete.description: Removes a person from the team. A caller who names their own id leaves the team, and the team's last admin cannot be removed.

parameters.description: The id of the person to remove.
parameters.name: user_id

patch.description: Sets the member's role on the team. The team's last admin cannot be demoted. Multi mode only.

post.description: Restores an archived team so it can be seen and changed again, and returns it. The agent runs and conversations the archive ended stay ended. Only an organization admin may call it, and a team that is not archived is refused. Multi mode only.

get.description: Returns the team's LLM spend over the window, in USD, with its totals by category, event handler, model, and UTC day. The totals by person are included only for a team admin.

parameters.description: The team's id, or default for the one team in local mode.
parameters.name: team_id

parameters.description: Start of the window, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight; with since and until both absent the window is the current UTC calendar month up to now, and with only one of them given the other end is open.
parameters.name: since

parameters.description: End of the window, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp or a YYYY-MM-DD date read as UTC midnight, which must be after since when both are given.
parameters.name: until

get.description: Upgrades the connection to a websocket that streams events for the caller in their current organization, such as a changed task list or a run's new messages. Most events say only that a resource changed, and the client reads it again through its route.
